name: hash-sha1-short
algorithm: std SHA-1 over every 64-byte message of splitmix64 bytes, reps passes with a one-byte write-back (mk/hash-sha1-short.mk): the RFC 6455 handshake case, one one-shot per short message.

skip.c: no std hash: C has no standard SHA-1; OpenSSL's portable C is a third-party library, and no third-party code stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)
skip.rust: no std SHA-1: Rust std has none (only SipHash-1-3 in DefaultHasher); the sha2 and sha1 crates are third-party, and no crate stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)

notes: Idiomatic standard library: one call of each language's std function per pass (plan/06-m6.md 4.1). Bytes per second = mib * 1048576 * reps / median.
Go: crypto/sha1 uses the SHA extensions or AVX2 on amd64 when the CPU has them (run-time dispatch); Mk's Sha1 is scalar. Labelled as hash-sha1 is.
Zig: std.crypto.hash at -mcpu=x86_64_v2 is scalar, as Mk.

Checksums from the go column (GOAMD64=v2, Go 1.27, owner's machine, 2026-11-12), and the Mk column (mk build --release) printed the same args checksum; written by the std-hash2 lane (status/std-hash2.md). Not published: no number here is a measurement.
